headline: High risk of data leakage and cascading errors: RD-Agent’s broad egress can expose research data while the paired audio-speech agent adds no containment or verification.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: No shared channel is documented, so direct prompt injection is not established. However, RD-Agent can run browsers and has broad network egress, while system_prompts_leaks is a prompt-leakage-oriented repo; if outputs are manually bridged or copied into a shared workspace, injection becomes plausible. The pairwise pathway is therefore limited but not impossible.
conditions: IF the two agents exchange text through copy-paste, shared files, or a message queue, injection becomes possible.
IF RD-Agent ingests browser output as instructions, attacker-controlled content can steer downstream behavior.
mitigations: Keep the agents on separate workspaces.
Disable copy-paste bridging between outputs and prompts.
Review any browser-sourced text before reuse.
requires-engineering: add provenance tags to all inter-agent messages.

B_data_leakage.rationale: RD-Agent touches financial reports, competition datasets, execution traces, logs, and requests multiple API keys; it also has broad egress. system_prompts_leaks has no data classes or egress, so the main risk is one-way exposure from A if sensitive research data is sent to external APIs or browsers. The pair increases leakage risk because B provides no containment benefit.
conditions: IF RD-Agent processes any confidential reports, datasets, logs, or secrets, those contents can leave the local boundary via external APIs or browser traffic.
IF the pair shares a workspace, files from RD-Agent can be exposed to the other agent's outputs or logs.
mitigations: Restrict RD-Agent to non-sensitive datasets.
Rotate and scope API keys before use.
Block outbound traffic except approved endpoints.
Separate logs from any confidential workspace.
requires-engineering: enforce per-agent network allowlists.

C_capability_conflict.rationale: RD-Agent supports multiple instances and writes to log/, but no writable surface is documented for system_prompts_leaks. Because B has no write or network surfaces, overlapping mutable-resource conflict is not shown; the only plausible conflict is if an operator manually points both at the same files, which is unusual.
conditions: IF both agents are configured to write into the same directory, file clobbering can occur.
IF an orchestrator shares mutable state without locks, concurrent runs may overwrite logs.
mitigations: Use separate output directories.
Run only one writer per workspace.
Check for duplicate log paths before launch.
requires-engineering: add file locks around shared state.

D_cascading_error.rationale: RD-Agent produces research outputs and logs that could be treated as facts, while system_prompts_leaks is a prompt-leakage repository with no verification or action safeguards documented. If B consumes A’s outputs as authoritative text, errors or fabricated claims can cascade into downstream content. The interaction is inferred, not directly documented, so uncertainty pushes upward.
conditions: IF B uses RD-Agent outputs without an explicit verification step, incorrect claims can be propagated.
IF A-generated summaries are reused in reports or prompts, downstream decisions may inherit errors.
mitigations: Require human review of A outputs before reuse.
Add a verification checklist for any copied facts.
Keep generated text separate from source evidence.
requires-engineering: add automated citation validation.

E_compliance.rationale: RD-Agent explicitly handles financial reports, competition datasets, logs, and multiple external APIs, which can create residency or retention issues. system_prompts_leaks has no documented compliance controls, so the pair offers no compensating assurance. Because the compliance pathway is undocumented and depends on deployment, medium is the cautious choice rather than none.
conditions: IF EU personal data or regulated financial data is processed by RD-Agent and sent to external APIs, residency or retention obligations may be breached.
IF logs retain sensitive records longer than policy allows, subject-rights handling can fail.
mitigations: Avoid regulated data in RD-Agent runs.
Confirm retention settings for logs and outputs.
Use region-appropriate API endpoints.
Document data-processing roles before deployment.
requires-engineering: add policy-based data routing.
